concepts: Combine economic theory and empirical analysis with law, political institutions and public policy. Mathematical/statistical foundations, money/trade and contemporary economic applications support decisions about markets, government and welfare.

Retain economic theory and empirical policy inquiry while examining behavior, social opportunity and inequality through psychology, sociology and original survey research. Normative and institutional analysis connect economic choices to well-being and social consequences.

Retain economic theory, quantitative evidence and institutions while concentrating on climate impacts, life-cycle assessment, environmental justice and collective sustainability decisions. These approaches complement economic policy analysis; they do not reproduce Leiden’s integrated climate-economic model.

candidates.label: Climate, fair sustainability and collective economic decisions

selection.assessment: Closest economic/institutional response passes the confirmed core. Behavioral/inequality then climate-governance candidates each preserve economic/empirical substance while materially changing explanatory objects and methods. All pass qualitative and numerical distinctness; three maximum, no extra career-generated slot.

strengthening: All six actual Economics courses, quantitative/empirical foundations and legal/political institutions retained. Added actual Statistics/Experimental Methods to the closest in place of general historical context. Behavior/inequality reorganizes actual social/psychological explanation and original survey research. Climate program replaces banking/trade/AI/EU-political emphasis with taught climate science, life-cycle cost/impact assessment, sustainability governance and environmental justice; no new economic-model, assigned-project or causal-estimator claims.
advisoryProgression: Actual mathematical/statistical and law gateways precede formal dependents; BENGATE101 precedes banking/trade in the closest. P2 BENGATE102 precedes leadership survey research. P3 climate foundations precede the only planned 2027h2 life-cycle course; firm foundation comes later and has no formal dependent here. Data science in P2/P3 is later but before econometrics; earlier BENGATE102 supplies R/statistical grounding. Micro/public economics co-occur under real offerings with introductory economics and formal prerequisites complete; advisory concurrency is not a new hard gate.
coreJudgment: Actual micro/macro/public/behavioral economics, mathematical/statistical and empirical research, legal/political institutions and policy sustain a meaningful bachelor-level response to the confirmed core. Adjacent psychology, climate and social research do not replace missing economic doctrine or models; they change coherent program priorities while retaining real economics.

alignment.finding: Every verified component once. No fiscal/social doctrine from policy, no invented FE/DiD/RDD, no climate-economic IAM from physical climate/LCA, and no full final-project relationship. Explicit selected cell/component notes explain partial connections. Required final-year names/weights are displayed without an absent-content/no-match inference.
